goal_pairs.title: Cap-level Euclidean enclosure at |tau|=1e-8 via second-order local expansion and a smooth spectral kernel
goal_pairs.model: Zero-selected patterned AQ subfamily (selected triple (0,0,0), 21 omitted faces per anchor at alpha*tau/24, whole-star boundary, tau=+1e-8, both signs as a control), AQ1 subsequential state omega_num, physical clock s=alpha*t_E/hbar, s=1 and the AT6 grid 0<=s<=128 as a second target
goal_pairs.observable: C(s)=<chi,e^{-sH/alpha}chi>, chi=(W-omega(W))Omega for the original xz Wilson loop W, plus omega(W) and omega(W^2)
goal_pairs.control: (1) Poisson-kernel replay must reproduce the 1.2651e-6 floor; (2) a kernel without the x>=0 agreement (f != e^{-sx} on part of [0,inf)) must be rejected; (3) an observable with nonvanishing first order (omega(W) itself, tau/144) must show the O(tau) term; (4) sign flip tau -> -tau must leave C(s) unchanged at O(tau) and change omega(W) sign; (5) dropping the left-eigenvector correction l-Omega_0 must be detected as a normalization error on a four-site fixture
expected_outcome_types: insufficient (anchored bound for the left eigenvector not proved; fallback to sqrt reset)
goal_pairs.why: Removes both bottlenecks named in the brief: the sqrt state bound (Riesz-projection expansion omega_N(A)=<l,e^{C}Ae^{-C}Omega_0>) and the Poisson log floor (smooth-extension kernel, M_1~3). Selection rules make the whole budget O(tau^2), estimated ~1.5e-9 at the cap with AM2's majorant constants.

goal_pairs.title: Certified sign and size of an interaction effect on the exact two-plaquette finite graph
goal_pairs.model: Round11 coupled two-plaquette SU(2) graph (7 links, 6 vertices, physical quotient variables x,y,z, constant Haar density on the constrained body), alpha=1, kappa_i=lambda_i/alpha in {(1,0),(1,1),(1,2),(2,2)}, polynomial degree cutoff D in {6,8} with the exact omitted-degree tail threshold and strict R gate; explicitly a different finite model (kappa=tau/24 in the AL1 dictionary, i.e. tau in [24,48])
goal_pairs.observable: <x> (plaquette-1 Wilson expectation) and the two-body shift delta=<x>_{kappa1,kappa2}-<x>_{kappa1,0}
goal_pairs.control: (1) kappa_2=0 must reproduce the Round10 one-plaquette enclosure; (2) dropping the shell-(D+1) residual leakage must be rejected; (3) a wrong-gap input (E_1 lower bound below mu) must fail the Davis-Kahan step; (4) an inertia count at an exact repeated eigenvalue; (5) python-flint fmpq_mat replay must agree bit-for-bit with the Fraction admission values
expected_outcome_types: accepted_within_scope (both <x>>0 and delta sign certified at D=8)
insufficient (residual widths exceed delta at D<=8)
goal_pairs.why: The only executable route to an enclosure that excludes the free reference: on the Z^3 family the first-order shift of C(s) vanishes and the mean shift tau/144 is 6.9e-11 at the cap. One-plaquette preview (N=8 characters, Fractions, 0.03 s): kappa=1 gives <W> in [0.1576,0.1639]; matrix sizes 84 (D=6) and 165 (D=8).

goal_pairs.title: Boundary-family comparison for the AQ limiting states (statement and derivation only)
goal_pairs.model: Two finite-volume families at |tau|<=1e-8: centered whole-star boxes (AQ1) versus all-contained-face boxes (AL1's padded prescription), local observable class B(H_R) for fixed R, common clock
goal_pairs.observable: sup over ||A||<=1 in B(H_R) of |omega_N^{(1)}(A)-omega_N^{(2)}(A)| as a function of dist(R, boundary)
goal_pairs.control: (1) at tau=0 both families give the Haar product exactly; (2) the bound must not depend on |Lambda|; (3) a fixed-volume comparison must not be relabelled as uniqueness of the thermodynamic state
expected_outcome_types: statement with explicit hypotheses (weighted anchored norm, Yarotsky-type decay rate)
goal_pairs.why: Goal 4 needs a rate; (M1) plus a weighted anchored norm would give one, and the missing weight is the same unproved step as in AV, so the derivation is shared.

goal_pairs.title: Regulator/coupling dictionary and the one uniform estimate (statement only)
goal_pairs.model: AL1 dictionary a, g^2, alpha=g^2/(2a), lambda=2/(g^2 a), tau=96/g^4, delta=alpha/8, hbar, E_star fixed; Euclidean comparison rows: Cao-Nissim-Sheffield 't Hooft regime, Gauvin fixed-cutoff SU(3), Chatterjee Yang-Mills-Higgs Gaussian limit
goal_pairs.observable: The volume-uniform gap alpha/16=g^2/(32a) for g^4>=9.6e9 and its non-uniformity along a->0, g(a)->0
goal_pairs.control: (1) every parameter classified (regulator/coupling/state preparation/measured/deformation) with units; (2) the AL1 all-n failure path reproduced; (3) no fraction of the continuum problem stated
goal_pairs.why: Goal 5's proposed first-loop test is exactly this statement; it costs no loop and fixes what later loops may claim.

strategy_changes: Replace the Poisson kernel by a smooth-extension kernel f=e^{-sx} on x>=0 with a C^2 (or smoother) taper on [-a,0] for every real-time-to-Euclidean transfer; evaluate f-hat in closed form with directed rounding; no cutoff L.
Count perturbative order by selection rules (Haar single-occurrence orthogonality, center symmetry) before writing an error budget; budget at O(tau^2) where first order vanishes.
Use the Riesz-projection identity omega_N(A)=<l,e^{C}Ae^{-C}Omega_0> for local expectations from AM2's expansion instead of the variational reset; the reset stays as a control.
For the shift goal, move to either the mean omega(W_p) (first order tau/144) or the exact finite graph; stop targeting C(s) shifts at first order.
Adopt python-flint (fmpq_mat, arb) as the independent reverse implementation and cross-check; keep stdlib Fraction arithmetic as the sole admission arithmetic.
Freeze the Gauvin v1/v3 diff and the AQ1/AM2 family identity as declared premises before AV production.

skill_updates.content: Kernel smoothness at the spectral edge determines the real-time moment needed; e^{-s|x|} costs a log cutoff, a smooth extension costs a constant. Vanishing first-order terms must be proved by a symmetry/orthogonality rule and then exploited with a second-order remainder.
Before any AM2 novelty statement, diff arXiv:2503.15539 v1 against v3 for Theorem 2.3 and record which constants (radius, J/delta, on-site gap) differ from AM2's.
Record proxy-blocked or paywalled primary records as leads with the HTTP status; a search-summary depth is never promoted to a read section.

disagreements: Brief observation 3 assumes the interaction shift is O(tau); for C(s) and omega(W^2) it is O(tau^2) by selection rules, so route (b) needs a third-order remainder and route (a) or the mean omega(W) is the honest target.
Brief observation 2 treats the 1.2-1.3e-6 floor as a property of the real-time comparison; it is a property of the Poisson kernel and disappears with a smooth-extension kernel.

Brief observation 1 targets O(tau) constants c_1,c_2; for W^2 and for W alpha^0_theta(W) the honest target is O(tau^2), while for omega(W) the exact first-order coefficient 1/144 should be stated rather than a crude c_1~1800.
AM2's novelty relative to Gauvin v3 Theorem 2.3 is unverified; the ledger flags the version history (v2/v3 dated 2026-09-11/14) and the physics.gen-ph category as provenance facts, not judgments.
open_questions_for_skeptic: Is an anchored-norm bound for the left eigenvector l provable with AM2's unweighted anchored norm, or is a support-size weight w^{|I|} unavoidable? Provide a damaging example if the unweighted bound fails.
Are AQ1's centered whole-star boxes exactly AM2's Hamiltonian family (same retained stars, same on-site reference), so that finite-volume local bounds pass to omega_num along AQ1's subsequence?
Does the relative-unitary Dyson argument of AT4 extend to second order with unbounded on-site terms without new domain assumptions?
Do faces sharing two links with W (same-plane neighbours) or the W face itself produce any nonzero first-order term? (Predicted: none, by <W^3>_Haar=0 and single-occurrence orthogonality.)
Which constant J_0 should be frozen for the uniform model (J=29|tau|), and does the AM2 combinatorics accept support-1 selected terms with p_max=4 unchanged?
Does the finite-graph delta on the Round11 two-plaquette model satisfy the roadmap's meaning of 'an interaction-induced effect', given the explicit different-model label?
Did Gauvin arXiv:2503.15539 v1 (2025-03-06) already contain the fixed-cutoff creation-expansion gap (Theorem 2.3 in v3)?
